advances: The specified two-block capped-composition family has one capacity surplus exponential in its full intrinsic rank, uniformly over all source tilts and their boundary limits. Conditioning on the three block totals costs at most a factor nine in the capacity second moment. The accepted simplex surplus pays this cost in all sufficiently large ranks; one fixed finite-family face-conditioning argument handles the remaining ranks, including the dilation-one slices at k=2. This is a capacity certificate for this family, not a support-independent capacity assertion or an actual-depth moment theorem.
author: research-agent
proof:
First establish the lattice geometry. In \(H_k\), consider the polytope of real nonnegative vectors with \(k-1\le S_A\le k+1\). For a point \(\mathbf N\) of this polytope, write \(s=S_A(\mathbf N)\), \(a=k-1\), and \(b=k+1\). Both \(s\) and \(2k-s\) are positive. For \(t=a,b\), form \(\mathbf N^{(t)}\) by multiplying its first block by \(t/s\) and its second block by \((2k-t)/(2k-s)\). These two points have first-block totals \(a\) and \(b\), respectively, and
\[
\mathbf N=\frac{b-s}{b-a}\mathbf N^{(a)}
          +\frac{s-a}{b-a}\mathbf N^{(b)}.
\]
At either endpoint total \(t\), the real slice is a product of two composition simplices. Its vertices are \(t\mathbf e_i+(2k-t)\mathbf e_j\), with \(i\in I_A\), \(j\in I_B\). All these vertices are integral and belong to \(J_k\). The preceding convex combination therefore proves that the real polytope is \(\operatorname{conv}J_k\). Its lattice points are exactly \(J_k\), proving completeness. The point \((1,\ldots,1)\) has all coordinates positive and satisfies the cap inequalities strictly, so the affine hull is all of \(H_k\), of dimension \(R=2k-1\).

Deleting \(N_{2k}\) is an affine lattice bijection from \(H_k\cap\mathbb Z^{2k}\) to \(\mathbb Z^{2k-1}\): its inverse appends \(N_{2k}=2k-\sum_{i=1}^{2k-1}N_i\). The difference lattice has basis \(\mathbf e_i-\mathbf e_{2k}\), \(1\le i\le2k-1\), and is the kernel of the integer sum map. In particular it is saturated. The block-total functional takes value one on \(\mathbf e_1-\mathbf e_{2k}\), so it is primitive on this difference lattice.

For each allowed integer \(s\), the slice affine hull has the two equations \(\sum_{i\in I_A}N_i=s\), \(\sum_{i\in I_B}N_i=2k-s\). A point with coordinates \(s/k\) in the first block and \((2k-s)/k\) in the second block is strictly positive, so the slice rank is exactly \(2k-2=R-1\). Its full affine lattice is parametrized by
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf x&=(N_1,\ldots,N_{k-1}),
&N_k&=s-\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}x_i,\\
\mathbf y&=(N_{k+1},\ldots,N_{2k-1}),
&N_{2k}&=2k-s-\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}y_i.
\end{aligned}
\]
The chart and its inverse are integral affine maps, and nonnegativity is precisely \(\mathbf x\in D_{s,k-1}\), \(\mathbf y\in D_{2k-s,k-1}\). This proves the asserted exact lattice product and slice completeness. Equivalently, its difference lattice is the saturated kernel of the primitive block-total functional within the original difference lattice.

Capacity is unchanged under these charts. In the full chart, every intrinsic linear functional extends to \(\mathbb R^{2k}\) by assigning coefficient zero to \(N_{2k}\). In the slice chart, an ambient coefficient vector \(\mathbf u\) restricts to the intrinsic coefficients \(u_i-u_k\) in the first block and \(u_{k+i}-u_{2k}\) in the second block, for \(1\le i\le k-1\). Conversely, any pair of intrinsic coefficient vectors extends by setting \(u_k=u_{2k}=0\). Thus every intrinsic normal extends, including at boundary target points; no attainment of an exponential infimum is needed. This is the affine invariance used in bf1ff94487296374.

Let \(\lambda_s:=p_{\boldsymbol\ell}(J_{k,s})\), and write \(p^{(s)}:=p_{\boldsymbol\ell}(\,\cdot\mid J_{k,s})\). Here \(\lambda_s\) is a slice mass, distinct from the vertex coefficients \(\lambda^{A,B}_{\mathbf v}\) and their bound \(\lambda_A\). All three masses are positive and sum to one. Substitution in the slice chart gives
\[
\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf N
 =\ell_k s+\ell_{2k}(2k-s)
  +\boldsymbol\theta^{(A)}\cdot\mathbf x
  +\boldsymbol\theta^{(B)}\cdot\mathbf y.
\]
The constant factor cancels in the conditional normalizer. Hence \(p^{(s)}\) is exactly the product of the normalized simplex laws with the displayed parameter ratios, using the formula of 609407d6db81b18b and with no modification of the source or target law. For dilation one this probability formula is a definition only, not an invocation of that fact's capacity gain.

For a product law in these independent charts, the centered exponential sum factors into its two centered exponential sums. Taking the infimum over the two independent vectors gives the product of the capacities: each sum is at least its own positive infimum, and vectors approaching both infima give the reverse inequality. Summation with the product target probabilities then gives the product of the two capacity moments. This is also the identity (30) of bf1ff94487296374. If \(k\ge3\), both dilations \(s\) and \(2k-s\) are at least \(k-1\ge2\), so 609407d6db81b18b applies to both factors. Consequently
\[
\mathcal B_2(p^{(s)})
 \ge g_{\mathrm{simplex}}^{2k-2}4^{-(2k-2)}
 =g_{\mathrm{simplex}}^{R-1}4^{-(R-1)}.
\]

Fix \(\mathbf j\in J_{k,s}\). For every original ambient normal \(\mathbf u\), retaining the terms on its slice gives
\[
\sum_{\mathbf N\in J_k}p_{\boldsymbol\ell}(\mathbf N)
 e^{\mathbf u\cdot(\mathbf N-\mathbf j)}
 \ge\lambda_s\sum_{\mathbf N\in J_{k,s}}p^{(s)}(\mathbf N)
 e^{\mathbf u\cdot(\mathbf N-\mathbf j)}
 \ge\lambda_s\mathsf C_{p^{(s)}}(\mathbf j).
\]
Taking the original infimum proves \(\mathsf C_{p_{\boldsymbol\ell}}(\mathbf j)\ge\lambda_s\mathsf C_{p^{(s)}}(\mathbf j)\). The normal-extension property above ensures that the conditional capacity here is precisely the intrinsic slice capacity. Since the original target probability on this slice is \(\lambda_s p^{(s)}(\mathbf j)\), summing the squared comparison over all three slices yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal B_2(p_{\boldsymbol\ell})
 &\ge\sum_{s=k-1}^{k+1}\lambda_s^3\mathcal B_2(p^{(s)})\\
 &\ge g_{\mathrm{simplex}}^{R-1}4^{-(R-1)}
       \sum_{s=k-1}^{k+1}\lambda_s^3\\
 &\ge\frac19g_{\mathrm{simplex}}^{R-1}4^{-(R-1)}
 \qquad(k\ge3).
\end{aligned}
\]
The final inequality is \((\lambda_{k-1}+\lambda_k+\lambda_{k+1})^3\le9\sum_s\lambda_s^3\). Thus
\(4^R\mathcal B_2(p_{\boldsymbol\ell})\ge(4/9)g_{\mathrm{simplex}}^{R-1}\). For \(R\ge R_0\), necessarily \(k\ge3\), and
\[
\log\frac{(4/9)g_{\mathrm{simplex}}^{R-1}}{g_0^R}
 =\left(\frac R2-1\right)\log g_{\mathrm{simplex}}-\log(9/4)
 \ge0.
\]
This proves \(4^R\mathcal B_2(p_{\boldsymbol\ell})\ge g_0^R\) in every large rank.

The remaining ranks are exactly \(2\le k\le K_0\). Their central slices already supply more than \(2^R\) points. Indeed, the number of nonnegative compositions of \(k\) into \(k\) coordinates is \(\binom{2k-1}{k-1}\), so
\[
\begin{aligned}
|J_k|&\ge\binom{2k-1}{k-1}^{\!2},\\
\binom{2k-1}{k-1}
 &=\prod_{i=1}^{k-1}\frac{k+i}{i}
 \ge3\,2^{k-2},\\
|J_k|&\ge9\,4^{k-2}
 =\frac98\,2^{2k-1}>2^{2k-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The first product factor is \(k+1\ge3\); each remaining factor is at least two. This argument includes \(k=2\), where there are no remaining factors.

We now prove that the finite-family constants stated above apply to these supports, using only the capacity parts of bf1ff94487296374. The construction follows the capacity face-transfer argument in 0114546e99a0a84c, with its family of pyramid supports replaced by the present \(\mathscr A\), its ranks replaced by \(r_A=2k-1\), and its \(\lambda_A,\eta,g_{\mathrm{small}}\) specialized exactly as specified in the statement.

For each nonempty \(B\subseteq A\), its average \(\mathbf b_B\) lies in the relative interior of \(F_A(B)\). A supporting functional tight at the average must be tight at every point of \(B\); a proper face containing that average would therefore contain \(B\), contradicting the minimality of \(F_A(B)\). Every relative-interior point of a polytope admits a representation positive at every vertex: give each vertex a sufficiently small common positive coefficient and represent the remaining required point in the polytope. The feasible vertex-coefficient set in the definition of \(\lambda_A\) is compact, so the maximum of its smallest coefficient is attained and is positive. There are finitely many nonempty \(B\) and finitely many supports \(A\); hence each \(\lambda_A>0\), \(\eta>0\), and \(g_{\mathrm{small}}>1\).

Fix \(A=J_k\in\mathscr A\) and an arbitrary source tilt \(\boldsymbol\ell\), and denote its law by \(p\). Let
\(m_{\boldsymbol\ell}:=\max_{\mathbf x\in A}\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf x\), \(L:=\log(4M_A)\), and
\(B:=\{\mathbf x\in A:\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf x\ge m_{\boldsymbol\ell}-L\}\).
The scalar \(m_{\boldsymbol\ell}\) is the maximum score called \(m\) in the face argument (44)--(46) of bf1ff94487296374, not a simplex dilation. The normalizer is at least \(e^{m_{\boldsymbol\ell}}\), and the total numerator outside \(B\) is at most \(M_Ae^{m_{\boldsymbol\ell}-L}\). Thus \(p(B)\ge3/4\). Put \(F:=F_A(B)\), \(E:=A\cap F\), \(q_{\mathrm{face}}:=p(E)\), and \(\pi:=p(\,\cdot\mid E)\). These \(q_{\mathrm{face}},\pi\) are exactly the face mass \(q\) and conditional law \(\pi\) of that accepted face argument; in particular \(q_{\mathrm{face}}\ge3/4\).

In the chosen maximizing vertex representation, all coefficients are at least \(\lambda_A\), and
\[
\sum_{\mathbf v\in\operatorname{vert}F}
 \lambda^{A,B}_{\mathbf v}
 (m_{\boldsymbol\ell}-\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf v)
 =m_{\boldsymbol\ell}-\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf b_B\le L.
\]
Each summand is nonnegative. Every vertex of \(F\), and then every point of \(E\), therefore has score at least \(m_{\boldsymbol\ell}-L/\lambda_A\). The conditional normalizer is at most \(M_Ae^{m_{\boldsymbol\ell}}\), giving \(\pi_{\mathbf x}\ge e^{-L/\lambda_A}/M_A\ge\eta\) for every \(\mathbf x\in E\). This verifies precisely the hypotheses and bounds of (46) in bf1ff94487296374 for the present family.

The face support is complete: since \(A=\operatorname{conv}(A)\cap\mathbb Z^{2k}\), one has \(E=F\cap\mathbb Z^{2k}\), and \(\operatorname{conv}E=F\) because every vertex of \(F\) belongs to \(A\). Its intrinsic affine lattice is \(\operatorname{aff}(F)\cap\mathbb Z^{2k}\). This is an affine translate of a saturated lattice of rank \(\dim F\), since \(F\) has integral vertices. The conditional law is positive and log-affine on that complete support. Thus the intrinsic parity bound (5) and, when applicable, the quantitative strictness (7) of bf1ff94487296374 apply, including a zero-dimensional face.

For every \(\mathbf j\in E\), every mean-\(\mathbf j\) law on \(A\) is supported on \(E\). For a proper face, an exposing functional is maximal on \(F\) and strictly smaller on \(A\setminus E\); its expectation at \(\mathbf j\) forces all mass onto \(E\). For the full face this is automatic. On this common feasible set, \(p_{\mathbf x}=q_{\mathrm{face}}\pi_{\mathbf x}\), whence
\(D(\nu\|p)=D(\nu\|\pi)-\log q_{\mathrm{face}}\).
The entropy-capacity identity (2) of bf1ff94487296374, including its boundary-center assertion, proves the exact face identity
\[
\mathsf C_p(\mathbf j)=q_{\mathrm{face}}\mathsf C_\pi(\mathbf j),
\qquad
\mathcal B_2(p)\ge q_{\mathrm{face}}^3\mathcal B_2(\pi).
\]
There is one face-mass factor from the target probability and two from the squared capacity. This is a statement about the original capacity itself, not an invocation of the accepted actual-moment constant.

If \(F=\operatorname{conv}A\), then \(q_{\mathrm{face}}=1\), \(\pi=p\), and every atom is at least \(\eta\). Since \(M_A>2^{r_A}\), (7) of bf1ff94487296374 gives
\(4^{r_A}\mathcal B_2(p)\ge1+4^{r_A}\eta^3/4\ge g_{\mathrm{small}}\).
If \(F\) is proper, put \(t_F:=\dim F\le r_A-1\). The complete-face parity bound (5) gives
\[
4^{r_A}\mathcal B_2(p)
 \ge4^{r_A-t_F}q_{\mathrm{face}}^3
 \ge4\left(\frac34\right)^3
 =\frac{27}{16}\ge g_{\mathrm{small}}.
\]
Thus one fixed strict bound holds over all source tilts of every member of \(\mathscr A\). In particular no dilation-two-or-more assertion is required for any \(k=2\) slice.

For \(R<R_0\), one has \(k\le K_0\) and \(R\le R_{\max,\mathrm{small}}\), so
\(g^R\le g_{\mathrm{small}}^{R/R_{\max,\mathrm{small}}}\le g_{\mathrm{small}}\le4^R\mathcal B_2(p_{\boldsymbol\ell})\).
For \(R\ge R_0\), one has \(g^R\le g_0^R\le4^R\mathcal B_2(p_{\boldsymbol\ell})\). All constants are determined by the universal \(g_{\mathrm{simplex}}\) and one fixed finite family; they are independent of the variable \(k\) and every tilt. Both entries defining \(g\) exceed one, which proves the claimed single exponential surplus.

Finally, verify all boundary source-tilt limits with the same normalization. Fix \(k\), and let \(r_{J_k,\mathbf j}\) denote the unique maximum-entropy mean-\(\mathbf j\) law on \(J_k\), exactly the law \(r_{E,\mathbf j}\) of bf1ff94487296374 with \(E=J_k\). This law depends only on the support and the target. Log-affinity gives, for every mean-\(\mathbf j\) law \(\nu\),
\(D(\nu\|p_{\boldsymbol\ell})=-H(\nu)-\log p_{\boldsymbol\ell}(\mathbf j)\).
Here \(H(\nu):=-\sum_{\mathbf x:\nu_{\mathbf x}>0}\nu_{\mathbf x}\log\nu_{\mathbf x}\) is entropy. Applying (2) of bf1ff94487296374 gives the exact finite polynomial formula
\[
\mathsf C_{p_{\boldsymbol\ell}}(\mathbf j)
 =p_{\boldsymbol\ell}(\mathbf j)e^{H(r_{J_k,\mathbf j})},
\qquad
\mathcal B_2(p_{\boldsymbol\ell})
 =\sum_{\mathbf j\in J_k}
 p_{\boldsymbol\ell}(\mathbf j)^3e^{2H(r_{J_k,\mathbf j})}.
\]
This also holds at boundary target points for every positive source law; it does not assume that an ambient capacity minimizer exists.

Suppose \(p_{\boldsymbol\ell^{(h)}}\to p^\infty\), and put \(T:=\{\mathbf x\in J_k:p^\infty_{\mathbf x}>0\}\). To check the geometry of this limit rather than assume it, let \(F:=F_{J_k}(T)\), \(E:=J_k\cap F\), and \(\mathbf b_T:=|T|^{-1}\sum_{\mathbf x\in T}\mathbf x\). The same minimal-face argument above places \(\mathbf b_T\) in \(\operatorname{relint}F\). Consequently there is a probability \(\nu\) positive on all of \(E\) with mean \(\mathbf b_T\): give a sufficiently small common positive mass to all points of \(E\), and represent the remaining mean by vertices of \(F\). For every \(h\), affinity of the log probabilities yields
\[
\sum_{\mathbf x\in E}\nu_{\mathbf x}
 \log p_{\boldsymbol\ell^{(h)}}(\mathbf x)
 =\frac1{|T|}\sum_{\mathbf x\in T}
 \log p_{\boldsymbol\ell^{(h)}}(\mathbf x).
\]
The right side has a finite limit. All log probabilities on the left are nonpositive. If any point of \(E\) lay outside \(T\), its positive coefficient would force the left side to tend to minus infinity. Therefore \(E=T\). In particular the limit support is a complete face support in its saturated intrinsic affine lattice.

The restriction of \(\log p^\infty\) to \(T\) is affine: the restrictions of the preceding log probabilities converge to it, and the space of affine-function evaluations on a fixed finite set \(T\) is a closed finite-dimensional linear subspace. Thus \(p^\infty\) is a positive log-affine law on \(T\). For a target \(\mathbf j\in T\), the exposing-face argument forces every mean-\(\mathbf j\) law on \(J_k\) onto \(T\), so \(r_{J_k,\mathbf j}=r_{T,\mathbf j}\). The entropy-capacity identity on \(T\) therefore gives
\(\mathsf C_{p^\infty}(\mathbf j)=p^\infty_{\mathbf j}e^{H(r_{J_k,\mathbf j})}\).
In the finite polynomial formula, the terms with \(\mathbf j\notin T\) tend to zero and the others tend to the capacity-moment summands on \(T\). Hence
\[
\lim_{h\to\infty}\mathcal B_2(p_{\boldsymbol\ell^{(h)}})
 =\mathcal B_2(p^\infty)
 \ge g^{2k-1}4^{-(2k-1)}.
\]
Every sequence of positive source laws has a convergent subsequence on this finite support, and the argument applies to every such limit, including singleton and proper-face limits and arbitrary relative rates of diverging source tilts. No zero-weight parameter ratio or new target law is used. This completes the capacity certificate and all its boundary assertions.
statement:
All logarithms are natural. For each integer \(k\ge2\), let \(I_A=\{1,\ldots,k\}\), \(I_B=\{k+1,\ldots,2k\}\), and define
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_A(\mathbf N)&:=\sum_{i\in I_A}N_i,\\
J_k&:=\left\{\mathbf N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{2k}:
 \sum_{i=1}^{2k}N_i=2k,\quad k-1\le S_A(\mathbf N)\le k+1\right\},\\
H_k&:=\left\{\mathbf N\in\mathbb R^{2k}:\sum_{i=1}^{2k}N_i=2k\right\},
\qquad R:=2k-1.
\end{aligned}
\]
The symbol \(S_A\) is the specified block total, not the mixed-integer set \(S\) in the locked problem. The support variable \(A\) used below for the finite-family construction has the meaning of the support variable in bf1ff94487296374; it is not the block index set \(I_A\).

For arbitrary \(\boldsymbol\ell\in\mathbb R^{2k}\), equivalently arbitrary source weights \(w_i=e^{\ell_i}>0\), put
\[
\begin{aligned}
Z_{k,\boldsymbol\ell}&:=\sum_{\mathbf N\in J_k}e^{\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf N},
&p_{\boldsymbol\ell}(\mathbf N)&:=\frac{e^{\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf N}}{Z_{k,\boldsymbol\ell}},\\
\mathsf C_{p_{\boldsymbol\ell}}(\mathbf j)&:=\inf_{\mathbf u\in\mathbb R^{2k}}
 \sum_{\mathbf N\in J_k}p_{\boldsymbol\ell}(\mathbf N)
 e^{\mathbf u\cdot(\mathbf N-\mathbf j)},
&\mathcal B_2(p_{\boldsymbol\ell})&:=\sum_{\mathbf j\in J_k}
 p_{\boldsymbol\ell}(\mathbf j)\mathsf C_{p_{\boldsymbol\ell}}(\mathbf j)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
These are exactly \(\mathsf C_p\) and \(\mathcal B_2(p)\) of bf1ff94487296374 with support \(A=J_k\) and ambient dimension \(2k\); the assignment's \(B2\) is \(\mathcal B_2\), without rescaling. Their ambient definitions agree with the definitions in the intrinsic lattice chart below.

The support is complete in its saturated affine lattice \(H_k\cap\mathbb Z^{2k}\), has intrinsic rank \(R\), and has the integer chart obtained by deleting \(N_{2k}\). Each of the three slices
\(J_{k,s}:=\{\mathbf N\in J_k:S_A(\mathbf N)=s\}\), for \(s\in\{k-1,k,k+1\}\), is a complete primitive lattice slice of rank \(R-1=2k-2\). Deleting \(N_k\) and \(N_{2k}\) identifies it with
\(D_{s,k-1}\times D_{2k-s,k-1}\). Here \(D_{m,r}:=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^r:\sum_i x_i\le m\}\) for integers \(m,r\ge1\); for \(m\ge2\) this is exactly the support \(D_{m,r}\) of 609407d6db81b18b. At \(m=1\) the same notation is only a geometric extension, and no accepted simplex gain is asserted. Its conditional law is the product of the normalized exponential laws on these two supports, with parameter vectors
\[
\theta_i^{(A)}=\ell_i-\ell_k=\log(w_i/w_k),\qquad
\theta_i^{(B)}=\ell_{k+i}-\ell_{2k}=\log(w_{k+i}/w_{2k})
\quad(1\le i\le k-1).
\]
The parameter \(\theta\) in 609407d6db81b18b is \(\boldsymbol\theta^{(A)}\) for the first factor and \(\boldsymbol\theta^{(B)}\) for the second; its probability formula is used without rescaling, also to define the dilation-one conditional factors.

Let \(g_{\mathrm{simplex}}>1\) mean the single constant called \(g\) in 609407d6db81b18b. Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
g_0&:=\sqrt{g_{\mathrm{simplex}}},\\
R_0&:=\max\left\{6,\left\lceil
 2+\frac{2\log(9/4)}{\log g_{\mathrm{simplex}}}\right\rceil\right\},\\
K_0&:=\lfloor R_0/2\rfloor,
\qquad R_{\max,\mathrm{small}}:=2K_0-1,
\qquad \mathscr A:=\{J_2,\ldots,J_{K_0}\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The present \(g_0\) is a large-rank constant for this family, not the pyramid-specific value of \(g_0\) in 0114546e99a0a84c. Here \(R_0\) is an integer enlargement of the displayed logarithmic threshold, and \(\mathscr A\) is a single fixed finite family.

For \(A\in\mathscr A\), put \(M_A:=|A|\) and \(r_A:=\dim\operatorname{aff}(A)\). For every nonempty \(B\subseteq A\), let \(F_A(B)\) be the minimal face of \(\operatorname{conv}A\) containing \(B\), and let \(\mathbf b_B:=|B|^{-1}\sum_{\mathbf x\in B}\mathbf x\). Use the same maximum-of-the-smallest-vertex-coefficient selection as in 0114546e99a0a84c:
\[
\lambda_A:=\min_{\varnothing\ne B\subseteq A}
\max_{\substack{
 \lambda_{\mathbf v}\ge0\ (\mathbf v\in\operatorname{vert}F_A(B))\\
 \sum_{\mathbf v}\lambda_{\mathbf v}=1,\quad
 \sum_{\mathbf v}\lambda_{\mathbf v}\mathbf v=\mathbf b_B}}
\min_{\mathbf v\in\operatorname{vert}F_A(B)}\lambda_{\mathbf v}.
\]
All sums in this formula run over \(\operatorname{vert}F_A(B)\). For each \(B\), choose a maximizing representation and denote its coefficients by \(\lambda^{A,B}_{\mathbf v}\), exactly as in (11) of bf1ff94487296374. Thus \(\lambda_A\) is exactly the constant in (12) of that fact for those chosen representations. Set
\[
\begin{aligned}
\eta&:=\min_{A\in\mathscr A}
 \frac{\exp[-\log(4M_A)/\lambda_A]}{M_A},\\
g_{\mathrm{small}}&:=\min\left\{\frac{27}{16},
 \min_{A\in\mathscr A}\left(1+\frac{4^{r_A}\eta^3}{4}\right)\right\},\\
g&:=\min\left\{g_0,
 g_{\mathrm{small}}^{1/R_{\max,\mathrm{small}}}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\eta\) and \(g_{\mathrm{small}}\) mean respectively (12) and the constant called \(g\) in (14) of bf1ff94487296374, specialized to the present \(\mathscr A\). They are not the numerical constants obtained from the different pyramid family in 0114546e99a0a84c. Every member of the present family satisfies \(M_A>2^{r_A}\), so the inner minimum has no excluded members.

These finite formulas give \(g>1\), independent of \(k\) and all source weights, and
\[
\boxed{\mathcal B_2(p_{\boldsymbol\ell})
 \ge g^{2k-1}4^{-(2k-1)}
 \quad(k\ge2,\ \boldsymbol\ell\in\mathbb R^{2k}).}
\]
Moreover, for any fixed \(k\) and any sequence of source tilts whose laws converge to \(p^\infty\), the capacity moment converges to the capacity moment of \(p^\infty\) on its positive support, and the same inequality holds with the original rank \(2k-1\). That positive support is a complete face support of \(J_k\). Thus the assertion includes every boundary source-tilt limit, without taking ratios of zero source weights.
